AuroraCloud to provide sample customer reference and preferred region list by 2026-05-13

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-06 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood PM), Liam O'Connor (Aurora PM), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Integration Lead), Diego Morales (Aurora SA)

Summary (auto): Quick recap at top: align on marketplace listing requirements, reference arch diagrams, integration points (SSO/KMS/billing), and a perf validation plan.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, hi.
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Priya, hi all.
[00:12] Diego Morales: Diego on the call.
[00:14] Ethan Ross: Ethan from Redwood.
[00:16] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great. Goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing process and the technical integration for the joint reference architecture, and to agree next steps.

[00:34] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good, we want to make sure the listing is smooth and that the reference arch maps to our managed offerings. Also want to understand the private deployment options, VPC plumbing, and SSO.

[00:52] Priya Kapoor: Right, for some of our customers data residency and KMS integration are a hard requirement, so we'll need to confirm Redwood's KMS/HSM story for the listing.

[01:10] Ethan Ross: Yep, we can cover that. Quick note, apologies in advance if I mess up some product names - transcription often swaps things around - but our Dedicated and Private offerings support customer-managed KMS via KMS keys and a HSM-backed flow for on-prem. We'll share the security brief.

[01:30] Diego Morales: When you say share the brief, is that the SOC2/ISO paper or the implementation details? We need both ideally.

[01:42] Jordan Lee: We'll put both in the partner artifact bundle: the compliance summary and a tech appendix that shows config snippets for KMS, SAML, and RBAC.

[01:55] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. On the marketplace side, AuroraCloud requires a reference arch diagram plus a one-page solution brief and a test plan for performance claims.

[02:10] Maya Patel: Ok, our standard pack has a reference arch, a short customer-facing blurb, and an integration checklist. We'll tailor the diagram to show the Aurora managed VPC peering and the Redwood Private control plane option.

[02:28] Liam O'Connor: For billing, must double-check our metering model - we prefer partner-integrated billing rather than redirecting customers. Does Redwood support marketplace metering hooks?

[02:42] Ethan Ross: Yes, we have a metering API and a usage export that we can push to partner billing endpoints. There are a couple of modes - direct invoicing, or partner-billed via marketplace hooks. We should coordinate on how SKU mapping will look.

[03:03] Priya Kapoor: Can you send the SKU mapping example? Also, is there a way to restrict available models per region in the listing? Some of our regulated customers need model restrictions.

[03:18] Ethan Ross: We can restrict model catalog entries by region and customer segment in our backend; policy can be enforced via route-level RBAC and routing policies. We'll add a snippet to the tech appendix.

[03:34] Diego Morales: On the reference architecture, the important bit is the KV cache and autoscaling behavior - customers want to know expected latency under warm cache vs cold start. Can you provide bench numbers for both hosted and dedicated?

[03:52] Jordan Lee: We can provide representative numbers and a benchmark harness. For dedicated we show median p95 latency at X tokens for our standard 8-GPU pool, for hosted we show slightly higher variance but faster onboarding. We'll include sample outputs.

[04:12] Maya Patel: We propose a joint perf validation run: Aurora provides a staging environment and we run a 30k token workload to reproduce expected latencies and throughput; capture KV cache hit rates and token cost per request. Is that ok?

[04:28] Liam O'Connor: Yes that's fine. We'll need the test harness and steps.

[04:35] Ethan Ross: I'll prepare the harness and a Terraform snippet to spin up the test workers; and a CSV with metric outputs.

[04:46] Priya Kapoor: On security: SSO and SAML; Aurora requires SCIM user provisioning and SAML metadata exchange. Does Redwood support SCIM?

[04:58] Ethan Ross: Yes, Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 and SAML 2.0 SSO for enterprise accounts. For marketplace listings we normally include instructions on configuring SSO for the partner admin console.

[05:12] Diego Morales: Also need audit logs retention details - some customers ask for 7-year retention in the EU, how do you handle retention policies?

[05:22] Jordan Lee: For hosted we have configurable log retention tiers; for Private deployment customers can ship logs to their SIEM using Kafka or S3 and set any retention they need. We'll include the retention table.

[05:38] Maya Patel: Good - sounds like we can assemble the partner artifact bundle: listing draft, ref arch, security appendix, billing mapping, and perf plan. We'll share draft listing and pricing template by 2026-05-10.

[05:54] Liam O'Connor: On the listing copy - Aurora requires mention of support SLAs and a brief matrix of supported instance types. Can you include a table?

[06:06] Jordan Lee: We'll include a supported hardware matrix and a short FAQ for customers.

[06:18] Priya Kapoor: One integration question - do you have a marketplace-friendly image or containerized deployment for edge customers?

[06:28] Ethan Ross: For Private we provide a Helm chart and an installer image; for marketplace we can provide a reference container manifest that adheres to sponsor requirements.

[06:40] Diego Morales: There's sometimes confusion on model variants and quantization. Could the listing call out recommended quantized variants for latency-sensitive workloads?

[06:52] Ethan Ross: Yes, in the ref arch doc we can call out recommended model profiles, with quantization and expected token cost tradeoffs. We'll add a short table.

[07:05] Liam O'Connor: Regarding certifications - Aurora requires SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 for marketplace partners. Do you have current certificates?

[07:16] Jordan Lee: We have SOC2 and ISO certs; I'll attach the certs to the partner bundle.

[07:26] Priya Kapoor: Great - on timelines, Aurora has a marketplace intake cycle that reviews artifacts every two weeks; if we submit by 2026-05-10 we can target listing by end of May.

[07:38] Maya Patel: That aligns well. Next, let's quickly walk through a proposed reference arch - I'll screen-share the diagram (note: this is transcribed so screenshot references are brief).

[07:52] Maya Patel: Draft diagram: customer VPC with peered private link into Aurora managed network, Redwood Private control plane in the Aurora VPC with a dedicated GPU pool behind. Traffic flows, KMS integration, audit log sinks to customer's S3 - any objections?

[08:14] Diego Morales: Sounds right. For peering we prefer using AWS PrivateLink rather than classic VPC peering when possible. Can you support that?

[08:24] Ethan Ross: Yes, PrivateLink is supported; we have sample CloudFormation and Terraform snippets.

[08:36] Priya Kapoor: On the KMS flow, who holds the key? Customer or Aurora? Many of our customers want customer-owned keys.

[08:46] Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys; the control plane stores encrypted tokens but not raw model artifacts. We'll document the key rotation steps.

[08:58] Liam O'Connor: For the marketplace listing we should add a note about recommended support SLAs for enterprise customers - 24x7 on-call with 1 hour P1 response for critical incidents.

[09:10] Maya Patel: We can include SLA options in the pricing template - standard and premium.

[09:20] Diego Morales: A quick real question - have you integrated with Aurora's usage reporting? We need to match metering dimensions.

[09:30] Ethan Ross: We can map Redwood metrics (tokens in, tokens out, embeddings units, inference hours) to Aurora dimensions. I'll send a sample mapping CSV.

[09:42] Priya Kapoor: Please do - that'll be critical for our billing team.

[09:48] Maya Patel: Switching to joint solutions: we discussed a reference architecture for a customer-facing assistant + search product that uses Redwood embeddings + Aurora search. The joint solution doc should show flow: Redwood embeddings -> Aurora search index -> application. Any technical caveats?

[10:06] Diego Morales: Latency for embedding generation is a factor; recommend async ingestion and pre-warming for high QPS. We need to show a batching strategy.

[10:18] Ethan Ross: We have batching and caching recommendations in Redwood Optimize; we'll include a recommended batch size and cache TTL for typical workloads.

[10:28] Liam O'Connor: For the joint solution cert, can we co-brand the doc and have an Aurora-approved logo?

[10:34] Jordan Lee: Yes we'll follow Aurora's partner brand guidelines - we'll include the co-branding assets in the bundle.

[10:42] Priya Kapoor: Another item - legal. Our procurement team needs a sample MSA and data processing addendum. Do you have partner-friendly templates?

[10:52] Maya Patel: We have a partner MSA template and a standard DPA that supports EU data residency. I'll have legal drop those into the share.

[11:02] Diego Morales: For the perf validation, what metrics will you capture? We want p50/p95 latency, throughput (reqs/sec), KV cache hit ratio, and cost per 1k tokens.

[11:14] Ethan Ross: We'll capture exactly those metrics, plus model memory footprints and GPU utilization. We'll produce a CSV and a short dashboard sample.

[11:26] Liam O'Connor: For the test environment we can provide a staging Aurora account and a reserved instance pool for the duration. Is that sufficient?

[11:36] Ethan Ross: Yes, that'll work. We'll coordinate credentials via secure transfer.

[11:44] Priya Kapoor: Also, can Redwood provide a short demo script for the marketplace reviewers? They like a reproducible quickstart.

[11:54] Maya Patel: Absolutely, a 5-minute demo script and a one-click quickstart link.

[12:02] Diego Morales: FYI sometimes marketplace reviewers ask for logs showing successful SSO and provisioning during the demo. Please include a runbook snippet.

[12:12] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll add a runbook to the bundle.

[12:20] Liam O'Connor: Questions from my security coms - do you support FIPS endpoints or similar for Gov customers?

[12:30] Ethan Ross: We have FIPS-compatible TLS stacks for Private deployments; for hosted we can enable FIPS in specific regions on request.

[12:40] Priya Kapoor: Perfect.

[12:46] Maya Patel: Time check - we've covered most items. Quick recap of decisions: Redwood will assemble partner artifact bundle (listing draft, ref arch, security appendix, billing mapping, perf plan). Aurora will provide region list, compliance contacts, and staging account. Perf run targeted week of 2026-05-18.

[13:10] Liam O'Connor: Correct. Also Aurora will route legal templates to Redwood for review - procurement expects that by 2026-05-13.

[13:22] Priya Kapoor: I'll share compliance contacts and the preferred region list.

[13:28] Diego Morales: I'll coordinate with our SRE to provision the test pool.

[13:34] Maya Patel: Great - next steps and owners are in the action items. Any final questions?

[13:42] Liam O'Connor: One last thing - do you have a requirement around support onboarding training? We may want a 1-hour enablement for our support engineers.

[13:52] Jordan Lee: We can run a enablement session; suggest scheduling it the week after the perf validation.

[14:00] Priya Kapoor: Works for us.

[14:06] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the bundle link and the pricing template.

[14:12] Ethan Ross: I'll send the benchmark harness repo link and the sample CSV.

[14:18] Maya Patel: Ok I'll send calendar invites for the perf run and the enablement session.

[14:25] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.

[14:28] Priya Kapoor: Thanks.

[14:30] Diego Morales: Bye.

[14:32] Maya Patel: Bye.
